title: LLM Modules: Knowledge Transfer from a Large to a Small Model using Enhanced Cross-Attention
date: arXiv v1 12 February 2025 (the only version); code and weights released 11 to 13 February 2025

code.title: k-kolomeitsev/LLM-Modules (GitHub)
code.note: the whole method is one file, model.py (979 lines, MIT licence), plus the full model outputs the paper's Table 1 summarises (compare-responses-from-models.md). The same files and the 7.2 GB checkpoint are on Hugging Face (kkolomeitsev/llm-modules), where they sit behind an access request; the GitHub copy is open. About 25 minutes for model.py and the outputs

takeaway: Freeze Qwen2-1.5B, pass its last hidden states through two trainable cross-attention layers with an adapter and a gate, feed the result into a GPT-Neo-sized decoder trained on Bespoke-Stratos-17k reasoning traces: on two arithmetic prompts the pair writes R1-style reasoning that GPT-Neo trained alone does not.
verdict: Read it as an idea, not a result. The evidence is two hand-picked prompts, one sample each, graded by the author. The released code adds problems the paper does not mention: its cross-attention lets every position see later tokens during training, so the loss curves cannot show learning; once the training subset starts being redrawn, the validation set is mostly reused training data; the "small" model is initialised at random rather than from GPT-Neo-125M, and running the pair takes 1.14 times the parameters of the frozen model alone. The idea of a frozen model read by a trained adapter is sound; Flamingo and CALM show it working with real evaluations.

resources.t: How to Teach a Model to Reason Without Overtraining It, for Less Than $10
resources.n: the same work told informally, with what the paper leaves out: one NVIDIA L4 for about 5 hours, under 10 dollars, how the GPT-Neo controls were trained, and the reshuffle rule.

resources.t: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning, Section 2.2
resources.n: the careful version of "a frozen model, read through new cross-attention": gated cross-attention layers inserted into a frozen language model, the gate starting at zero so training begins from the unchanged model.

resources.t: LLM Augmented LLMs: Expanding Capabilities through Composition (CALM)
resources.n: two frozen models joined by trained cross-attention at several layers, evaluated on real benchmarks against fine-tuned baselines; the large anchor model reads the small one, the opposite direction.

resources.t: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
resources.n: the distillation this paper sets itself against: train a small student on a large teacher's softened outputs.
the bottleneck adapter the paper's "Adapter Block" copies (down, non-linearity, up, residual), here inserted into a frozen BERT.
the training data: 16,710 questions with DeepSeek-R1's reasoning traces and answers (math, code, science, puzzles), made for fine-tuning Qwen2.5 7B and 32B.

kb.n: 2025: the teacher behind both sides of the comparison. Bespoke-Stratos-17k is R1's reasoning traces, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B is a Qwen model fine-tuned on 800,000 of them.
adjacent in the same batch: a pretrained model read a second way, with small trained adapters and a learned mix.

kb.t: Trained Persistent Memory for Frozen Encoder-Decoder LLMs
kb.n: adjacent in the same batch: trainable memory attached to a frozen backbone instead of retraining it.
2021: the cheap way to adapt the large model itself, which the paper cites but never compares against.
2023: LoRA on a 4-bit frozen model; fine-tunes a 1.5B model on one small GPU, the missing like-for-like baseline.
2017: the encoder-decoder cross-attention (queries from one stream, keys and values from another) the Enhanced Cross-Attention is built from, and the causal mask it leaves out.
2019: cited by the paper for transfer learning; an encoder read by a decoder through cross-attention, trained end to end.
2021: the kind of frozen encoder later joined to language models by adapters (Flamingo, LLaVA).

topics.n: distillation, supervised fine-tuning on reasoning traces, adapters and parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
the Qwen2 and GPT-Neo families and how models are composed.
